perspective:
Harold’s available information/perspective:

- I am Harold Padilla, a project manager. I have a friendship/professional relationship with Arthur Begum, a police officer, and I often turn to him for advice.
- I felt frustrated and anxious because my project team seemed unmotivated, and it was affecting our progress. I arranged to meet Arthur at a local coffee shop.
- I told Arthur my team seemed completely unmotivated and I was at my wits’ end. Arthur advised me to understand what drives each team member individually, have one-on-one conversations, and help people feel valued and understood. I said I had focused mainly on goals/deadlines but would try this. I felt more hopeful afterward.
- I decided to implement Arthur’s advice. I told my team we would have quick one-on-one chats to understand what motivates each of them. Team Member 1 said that could be helpful. Team Member 2 said they were open to it. I said I would schedule time with each of them and wanted us to make the project a success together.
- Later, I noticed the team still was not responding well to the new strategies. I felt disappointed and worried about the project’s future, so I discussed it with Arthur. I told him I had tried his suggestions but the team still wasn’t responding. Arthur said there might be deeper issues: personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that I might need to dig deeper. I said I would set up another round of meetings.
- Feeling determined and focused, I held one-on-one meetings and asked team members to share concerns or problems. Team Member 1 told me there was tension between a few people, affecting work. Team Member 2 told me they felt overwhelmed by the workload and stressed. I said I would look into resolving conflicts and see about redistributing tasks, and that their well-being was important to me.
- Feeling optimistic and empowered, I believed addressing individual concerns would improve team performance. I decided to create a more supportive and open environment through regular feedback sessions and team-building activities. I told the team this. Team Member 1 said it sounded great and would help us work better. Team Member 2 agreed and said it was good that concerns were being addressed. I said I was glad and that their input and well-being were crucial to our success.
